title: Deterministic Polynomial Factorization over Prime Fields
main_claim: Thm 1.1: there is a deterministic algorithm that completely factors dense f in F_p[x] in O(((n+1)log p)^{10^12}) bit operations. It rests on Thm 1.2, an algebraic reduction that runs in poly(B+E) time given auxiliary primes l_q ≡ 1 mod 12q such that p is not a q-th power mod l_q. Polynomially small auxiliary primes are obtained from the companion's uniform Hecke zero-free strip (Theorem 1.2 of the companion paper on primitive roots, fam 029), or under GRH.

issues.location: Sec 10, Theorem analytic:hecke (input from companion paper, OpenAIPrimitive26 Thm 1.2)
issues.description: The unconditional Theorem 1.1 depends entirely on the companion's claim that every finite-order Hecke L-function of every cyclotomic field containing mu_12 has no zero with Re s > 1-10^-6, uniformly. For K=Q(mu_12) this covers the Dedekind zeta function and so implies a quasi-Riemann hypothesis for zeta(s). That is far beyond known results, and this paper does not prove it. The paper discloses the dependence, and the dependence is not circular, because the companion does not use factorization. As a result, Thm 1.1's statement that it uses no GRH assumption is only as reliable as the companion's result. The GRH-conditional version follows from this paper alone.
issues.evidence: Sec 10 opening: 'Its proof is not part of this paper; all dependence on that paper is isolated in this input.' The family-029 board entry for rank 100 likewise names the uniform strip as the load-bearing, unverified input.

coverage: I read all 11 sections. Checked: (1) the geometric core, Sec 5. This covers the curve setup and genus; R ≅ Λ with λ injective on Λ and surjective on J; the T_t filtration lemma (injectivity, image = T_{t+1}[λ^t]); the ramification-generator and label lemma, re-derived via Hilbert 90, including the coefficient bookkeeping W' = W_0 + (Σa_i)∞_0 + (deg D_0)Σ∞_j and the sign of the label; the relation Σε_i = 0 via div Y; the Frobenius filtration argument (Π−1 lowers the filtration by 1, q lowers it by q−1, binomial induction to 1 + r(q−1)); finite-field descent; and the forced-separation ladder, where Ne lies in λ^{m-1}Λ but not λ^mΛ and the invariant propagates. I also ran a symmetry sanity check (X→ωX, Y→ωY on X^q−c): the τ-invariant label vector Σ iε_i is nonconstant, so there is no contradiction. (2) LambdaDivide: the norm promise via v_P(a_0) = b and Norm(Y) = F for odd q; the partial-sum maximum giving (1−σ)V = E. (3) The norm solver: the cyclic algebra splits under the promise; explicit local maximal orders at ramified, unramified (q | w and q ∤ w) and infinite places, including the commutation checks, the wrap-around entries and the (V')^q = u factor; the vector bundle on P^1, End-sections and the block upper-triangular fiber; the trace-kernel rank-one idempotent; b^q as the projector, via Cayley–Hamilton with char poly T^{q-1}(T−1); and the ansatz/valuation bounds. (4) Divisor arithmetic: the ideal representation, compression/pushforward, Riemann–Roch reduction, the simultaneous divisor sum (min-valuation generator argument) and circuit evaluation by leading coefficients. (5) UnitRoot (lifting-the-exponent, eigenvector order, unit search), the table construction (U_q is a degree-q field, V_q eigenvector with the q-part of ord u equal to q^{s+1}, ω_2 a nonsquare), the even-degree tournament (log shift of 2^{s-1}, row counts (N−1)/2), and the Berlekamp separator, driver and table induction (no circularity). (6) The analytic consequence: the discriminant bound O(B^3), the error B^{-17} at x = T·B^{2·10^7}, and the cancellation of completely split primes in Ψ_K − q^{-1}Ψ_M. (7) The W_t coefficient growth bound N(2q)^m. Not done: no machine experiment on actual curve and Jacobian arithmetic (no Sage/PARI available), and I only skimmed the complexity exponents in Sec 9.
sibling_notes: Family 142 had no prior entries. The companion (Primitive roots for every admissible integer base) is in family 029. That board's rank 100 and rank 248 entries both report no gap, but name the uniform cyclotomic Hecke zero-free strip (quasi-RH) as the load-bearing input that could only be checked for internal consistency. This paper's unconditional claim inherits that dependence exactly. Its algebraic reduction is independent of the companion and would, on its own, give GRH-conditional deterministic polynomial-time factorization. That is itself an extraordinary claim (a long-standing open problem), so independent expert review of Secs 3–7 is advised, even though I found no failing step.
